eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 105 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: UPDATE has to read before it writes
code:
UPDATE Production.Product
SET ListPrice = 25.00
WHERE ProductID = 680;
-- Step 1: find the row (a read)
-- Step 2: change it (a write)
caption: Two operations, back to back, on the same row.

eyebrow: The conversion deadlock, if S locks were used
code:
-- Session A: S lock to find row -- GRANTED
--            tries to upgrade to X -- WAITS
-- Session B: S lock, SAME row -- ALSO GRANTED
--            tries to upgrade to X -- ALSO WAITS
-- Neither releases first. Deadlock.
caption: Shared locks are mutually compatible — that's exactly the trap.

eyebrow: The U lock closes the trap
code:
-- U lock: compatible with S
--         NOT compatible with another U
--         NOT compatible with X
-- Only ONE session at a time can be "about to update."
caption: Two concurrent UPDATEs simply wait their turn — no deadlock.

eyebrow: U converts to X when the write proceeds
code:
-- sys.dm_tran_locks mid-UPDATE:
-- request_mode = 'U'  (briefly, while locating the row)
-- request_mode = 'X'  (once the write actually happens)
caption: U is the locate phase; X is the write phase that follows it.
